key_insight: Modeling children's tablet interaction trajectories with an AI-driven longitudinal digital phenotyping framework enables earlier, objective detection of atypical cognitive-motor development than static, one-off assessments.
problem_solved: Traditional screening for cognitive-motor atypicalities is subjective and episodic; this work provides a scalable, continuous, and objective method to capture developmental trajectories in children aged ~18 months–8 years using passive tablet-based interactions.
method: Longitudinal data collection via tablet interactions across multiple sessions/terms to capture within-child change over time.
Extraction of digital biomarkers from raw interactions (e.g., touch/gesture traces, timing, error patterns, movement smoothness, task complexity metrics).
Trajectory modeling and anomaly detection using time-series/longitudinal ML (normative growth curves, temporal models with interpretable outputs) to flag atypical development early.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a validated paradigm for continuous digital phenotyping that improves screening sensitivity and enables interpretable, data-driven early interventions—scalable to real-world deployments in pediatric monitoring and research.
visual_elements: Timeline infographic showing repeated tablet sessions per child and aggregated cohort follow-up periods.
Sample interaction visual: touch/gesture traces and heatmap from a tablet task comparing typical vs atypical patterns.
Normative trajectory chart with confidence bands and an individual child's trajectory highlighted, showing flagged deviations.
System pipeline diagram: data capture → feature extraction (digital biomarkers) → longitudinal model → clinician-facing alerts/visualization.
paper_title: Longitudinal Digital Phenotyping for Early Cognitive-Motor Screening
paper_authors: Diego Jimenez-Oviedo, Ruben Vera-Rodriguez, Ruben Tolosana, Juan Carlos Ruiz-Garcia, Jaime Herreros-Rodriguez
